content.rationale: Removal is where D14's guard (stnqmzuw), D7's rule that the removed node's own gates are abandoned with it (myprwuxt), D21's id refusal with its name and its excluded effects (tnqpoqxl, tsspuwzo, xtmprysl, qyynqqpx), the form's argument surface (the beyond-the-id refusal), the two refusals the scan forces (the unreadable node, the gate that evaluates beyond the node), the no-change case, the happy path (zrvnlzvw), the dependant refusal and its naming (wnxsoknq, zvtktmpz), O7-remove's silence (loxpnryv), S3-abandon's mechanism and S5-lifecycle's bracketing meet; this check drives the handler over a scratch jj workspace whose node files are named by real change ids and live in real changes, and pins each of those — including that no gate of the removed node is left behind — plus that the handler is the table's shape — a Verb row for it compiles (M-route). It reaches store_load through store_resolve, so it is a crate of its own. I1-serde (orrvsxqq) fixes the JSON layer the crate is written against — serde and serde_json, the crate's own `Value` and the derive — and I1-schema (zmmyomyp) fixes the validator these documents are checked with. It pins the read's refusal site (S2-read-refusal-site, vollyzvn): an unreadable node refuses before anything is abandoned.
